intro: Apollo 11 landed in Mare Tranquillitatis at 20:17 UTC on July 20, 1969 — the first crewed landing on another world. Armstrong and Aldrin spent 2h 31m outside the Lunar Module Eagle; Collins orbited in Columbia overhead. The crew returned 21.5 kg of lunar samples and left behind footprints, a retroreflector array (still used by Earth-based lasers), and a plaque: "We came in peace for all mankind".
